caption: The drawing features a single object resembling a stylized rooster, rendered in shades of muted brown and gray. The rooster is depicted in profile, facing left, with detailed plumage on its body, tail, and wings, indicated by curved lines and shading that give a three-dimensional effect. Its comb, beak, and eye are distinctly outlined, and the tail feathers are prominently arched and layered. The legs are fused into a single form, extending downward to merge into a rounded, textured base. The background of the drawing is plain and off-white, allowing the intricacy and coloration of the rooster-like object to stand out. The artist's name, "MICHAEL CROWHILL," is printed in small, clear letters near the bottom right of the drawing.
title: Weather Vane Finial
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
